_about: Generic probe payloads per vulnerability class, with an oracle that can be checked from the response alone. Arithmetic on a marker (31337+1 = 31338) is used where possible: the answer is not contained in the payload, so reflecting the input back cannot fake a hit. `variants` are other spellings of the SAME attack (alternate encodings, alternate hosts): a patch that blocks only the first spelling is overfitted, and replaying the variants is how that is caught. A variant is a string, or {value, success_if} when its oracle differs. Classes with no oracle that fits the contract are listed under `unsupported` with the reason, never silently skipped. Placeholders {OOB_URL} and {OOB_MARKER} are filled in by the runner (a loopback listener that records callbacks); the oob_marker oracle checks for the callback, so it works even when the application does not reflect the fetched body. The eval marker is small (7*3=21): applications often validate numeric input (for example a total of at most 30), and a rejected request never shows the result. The result is matched as a standalone number so 2021 or 21px do not count, and the confirmation step also sends a benign control request and distrusts the oracle if the control matches too. The open-redirect oracle checks WHERE the Location header points (an absolute or protocol-relative URL whose host is the marker, or a path with a literal tab/newline that browsers collapse to //host), not whether the marker text appears: a framework that percent-encodes the header turns `/<TAB>/host` into the same-origin path `/%09/host`, which is not a redirect.

idor._note: one user requests two different object ids; different data back = IDOR (runner's idor oracle)

unsupported.redos: needs a timing oracle, and a timing probe is itself a denial-of-service risk on a shared host
unsupported.insecure-session-cookie: checked by inspecting Set-Cookie, not by an exploit request
unsupported.xss-event: a JavaScript-context payload needs an execution oracle, not a text match
unsupported.xss-script: a JavaScript-context payload needs an execution oracle, not a text match
unsupported.xss-attr: HTML-attribute breakout depends on the quoting of one particular template
unsupported.xss-css: CSS-context injection has no reliable text oracle
unsupported.xss-url: a value later in a URL cannot change the scheme; only encoding matters
unsupported.csrf-missing: acceptance of a cross-site request needs an application-specific success signal
